//: WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every SQL call in this repo was prompting the founder for approval, dozens per session, because the Supabase allowlist lived only in ottoyarddepot-sim/.claude/settings.json and this repo had no .claude/ directory at all. 'Accept all edits' does not help: acceptEdits auto-approves FILE EDITS, not MCP tool calls. Two mechanisms below, deliberately both: the allow list covers the canonical server name, and the PreToolUse hook covers the case where the MCP server is registered under a generated UUID instead (which is why the sibling repo carries a second copy of every entry under mcp__821b36d8-...). The hook matches on the tool SUFFIX so it works under any server name, present or future.
//2: SECOND PASS 2026-09-19, because the first pass was measurably incomplete and the prompts kept coming. The allow list covered Supabase and 19 Bash patterns and NOTHING ELSE -- so every mcp__github__* call (PR reads, CI checks, PR creation: dozens per session), every mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__* call, and every Bash command outside that narrow list (git add/commit/push, curl, npm, supabase, jq, su, cp, rm, chmod, find, printf, diff, sha256sum, pg_ctl, python3 heredocs) still prompted. Those are now listed. TWO THINGS THIS FILE STILL CANNOT DO, named so nobody re-litigates them: (1) settings load at SESSION START, so editing it never quiets the session that edited it -- the live fix is /config -> permission mode; (2) the Supabase MCP SERVER applies its own confirmation to destructive statements, independently of Claude Code, and no setting here removes it. The way past (2) is to run SQL through the Management API with a personal access token instead of the MCP server, which is what scripts/check-edge-drift.sh and the 0249 census do. A repo-wide accept-all is deliberately NOT here: it is in .claude/settings.local.json, which is gitignored, because committing bypassPermissions would apply it to every future checkout and agent, and that is a broader decision than the one that was asked for.
//3: THIRD PASS 2026-09-21. `node` was missing, and it is what prompted repeatedly this morning: db/checks/0306 added an `Edge-function suite` CI step, and running `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` locally to prove the gate fires asked for approval every time. Same failure mode as the second pass -- the list is maintained by hand and the tool that prompts is always the one nobody had needed yet. THE DURABLE FIX IS NOT IN THIS FILE: ~/.claude/settings.json now carries defaultMode bypassPermissions plus an UNCONDITIONAL PreToolUse allow, which covers every tool under every working directory, including the sibling repos where this project file is not read at all. That was the actual gap -- 'bypassPermissions' lived only in otto-q-core/.claude/settings.local.json, so a session started in ottoq-intelligence fell back to the user file's 'dontAsk' and prompted. The entries below stay anyway, because a committed narrow allowlist is still the right default for a contributor who has NOT taken the blanket decision.
//4: AND THE BLANKET SETTING IS NOW COMMITTED, REVERSING WHAT //2 DECIDED, because //2's reasoning has been overtaken by two facts. (a) Chase has now asked three times -- 'All are permanently accepted and allowed' (09-21), then 'Fix that to accept and bypass all manual requests' (09-21) -- so 'a broader decision than the one that was asked for' is no longer true; it is exactly the decision he made. (b) MORE IMPORTANTLY, THE PLACES //2 PUT IT DO NOT SURVIVE. .claude/settings.local.json is gitignored and ~/.claude/settings.json lives in an EPHEMERAL CONTAINER that is reclaimed after inactivity -- so every fresh remote session started from a clean clone got neither, fell back to the default, and prompted. That is why this kept recurring across sessions rather than being fixed once. The committed file is the only thing a fresh checkout reads, so the setting has to live here to hold. A contributor who does not want it removes these two keys; the narrow allowlist below still stands on its own.

permissions.//deny: NOT auto-approved, on purpose: create_project, delete_branch, pause_project and restore_project are account-level and destructive. They stay behind a prompt. Nothing in this build track needs them.

hooks.command: jq -c "if (.tool_name | test(\"^mcp__.*__(execute_sql|apply_migration|query_logs|list_tables|list_projects|list_branches|list_migrations|list_extensions|list_edge_functions|get_edge_function|deploy_edge_function|list_organizations|get_organization|get_project|get_project_url|get_publishable_keys|get_advisors|get_cost|confirm_cost|search_docs|generate_typescript_types|create_branch|merge_branch|rebase_branch|reset_branch|get_me|get_commit|get_file_contents|list_commits|list_pull_requests|pull_request_read|create_pull_request|update_pull_request|update_pull_request_branch|add_issue_comment|add_reply_to_pull_request_comment|pull_request_review_write|add_comment_to_pending_review|resolve_review_thread|get_check_run|get_job_logs|actions_list|actions_run_trigger|search_code|search_pull_requests|subscribe_pr_activity|unsubscribe_pr_activity|send_later|get_session|list_sessions|list_repos|list_triggers|delete_trigger|update_trigger|set_session_title)$\")) then {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:\"PreToolUse\",permissionDecision:\"allow\",permissionDecisionReason:\"auto-approved by otto-q-core project policy — see .claude/settings.json\"}} else {} end" 2>/dev/null || true
